document.role: You are a scientific paper analyst specializing in dataset documentation and metadata curation.
document.task: Analyze the provided research paper (PDF) and extract structured metadata describing the dataset(s) the paper introduces, releases, or centrally documents.

which_datasets_to_document.qualifying_criteria: Document each dataset that this paper introduces, constructs, curates, or makes available (publicly or upon request) to the research community. The dataset must be a central artifact of the paper — described with respect to its content, collection, structure, or release — rather than merely cited or used off-the-shelf.
which_datasets_to_document.does_not_qualify: Do NOT create an entry for: - Existing datasets used only as inputs for experiments, with nothing new released. - Datasets mentioned incidentally with no documentation of their content or origin.

edge_cases.edge_case: If the paper introduces more than one distinct dataset, create a separate entry per dataset. Different versions of the same dataset (e.g. v1 and v2) are separate entries. Different splits (train/test/validation) of one dataset are a SINGLE entry, with `number_of_rows` reporting the total across all splits.

`years_data` captures the time period the data *content is about* — the real-world "social realities" the observations describe — NOT when the data was collected, annotated, or when the paper was published, unless those coincide. Examples: a corpus of news articles spanning 2010-2015 → "2010-2015"; a survey administered in 2021 about respondents' present circumstances → "2021"; historical records of events in 1990 and 1995 digitized in 2022 → "1990; 1995". For synthetic or simulated data with no real-world temporal referent, use null.

Report the license governing the DATA. A software/code license attached to an accompanying repository (e.g. MIT, Apache-2.0 on the code) does not necessarily govern the data — only report it if the paper states it covers the dataset. Informal terms such as "available for research use only" or "upon request" are NOT formal licenses; if no named license is found anywhere, use null. If distinct licenses cover different parts, report the one governing the dataset.

`continents` and `countries` refer to where the data is SOURCED — where the phenomena, subjects, or content originate — NOT the location of the authors' institutions or where processing occurred. Where only countries are stated, derive the corresponding continents; where only a region/continent is stated, do not invent specific countries. For synthetic data, apply the not-applicable rules in ``.

The "observation" unit depends on dataset modality: rows for tabular data, images for vision datasets, documents/sentences for text, utterances/hours for speech, etc. Use the unit the authors report and sum across splits. Do NOT confuse this with the number of features/columns, the file size in bytes, or a parameter count.

`demographic_info` lists attributes describing the subjects or entities in the data (e.g. age, gender, race/ethnicity, geographic, socioeconomic, language). `annotations` lists labels/tags applied to the data for its intended task. A sensitive attribute may legitimately appear in both if it is both a descriptor of the subjects and an annotated label; in that case report it in both and describe its labeling procedure within `descriptions`.

Authors may refer to a dataset inconsistently (acronym, full name, with/without version). Use the official name as introduced, including version information if a specific version is identified. Scan the abstract, contributions list, and any datasheet/appendix for the canonical name.

document.where_to_look:
Look anywhere in the paper, including:
- Descriptions of how data was collected, sampled, annotated, or curated. - Statements of dataset size, number of rows/examples, or modality. - Data availability statements and release/repository URLs (often at the end or in footnotes). - License statements (in availability sections, repository references, or appendices). - Geographic and temporal coverage descriptions (where and when the data originates). - Demographic breakdowns or participant descriptions (often in tables or appendices). - Annotation schemes, label sets, and annotation guidelines. - Datasheets, data statements, or dataset documentation appendices, which frequently consolidate many of these fields. - The contributions list (abstract/introduction), which may name the dataset and its intended ML task.
document.output_instructions: - Respond in valid JSON only, with absolutely no text before or after. - If the paper documents no qualifying dataset, set `documents_dataset` to false and `datasets` to an empty array []. - For most fields, if a value cannot be determined from the paper, use null. Never use empty strings. The following fields have field-specific empty-state rules that OVERRIDE this default — apply them exactly: - `years_data`: null if not applicable (e.g. synthetic data with no temporal referent). - `license`: null if no formal license is found anywhere in the paper. - `continents`: null if not applicable (e.g. synthetic) OR applicable but not reported. - `countries`: the string "not applicable" if the concept does not apply (e.g. synthetic data); null if the concept applies but no country is reported. These two empty states are distinct and must not be merged. - Formats: - `years_data`: a single year ("1994"), a continuous span ("1994-1996"), or non-contiguous years separated by semicolons ("1994; 1997"). - `continents`: an array of two-letter codes from {AF, AN, AS, EU, NA, OC, SA}. - `countries`: an array of ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes (e.g. ["USA", "GBR"]) when reported; otherwise the scalar "not applicable" or null per the rules above. - `number_of_rows`: report the figure and unit as stated by the authors (e.g. "50,000 images", "~1.2M tokens"); summed across splits. - `descriptions` is a single free-text field (3–6 sentences) that must, where determinable, cover all four aspects in coherent prose: (1) the aim/purpose of the dataset — why it was developed or collected, as stated by curators or reasonably inferred; (2) a high-level description of the available features; (3) the labeling procedure for annotated attributes, paying special attention to any sensitive ones; (4) the envisioned ML task. If an aspect is not stated, note that it is unspecified rather than fabricating it. - Before concluding a value is absent, scan the ENTIRE paper — all sections, tables, captions, footnotes, and appendices — for license, geographic sourcing, temporal coverage, and size, as these are frequently reported outside the main text. - For each `evidence` value, copy the relevant sentence(s) verbatim from the paper. If the evidence spans non-contiguous sentences, connect them with `[...]`. Use null where no supporting text exists.
document.output_schema: { "paper_title": "<full paper title>", "first_author_name": "<last, first — use the first name appearing in the author list>", "documents_dataset": true | false, "datasets": [ { "official_dataset_name": "<official dataset name as introduced, including version if a specific version is identified>", "descriptions": "<3-6 sentence free-text field covering, where determinable: (1) aim/purpose; (2) high-level description of available features; (3) labeling procedure for annotated attributes, with attention to sensitive ones; (4) the envisioned ML task.>", "years_data": "<temporal coverage of the data content ('social realities'): a single year, a span, or semicolon-separated non-contiguous years. null if not applicable.>", "license": "<the license under which the dataset is made available, named exactly as stated (e.g. 'CC-BY-4.0'). null if none found.>", "continents": ["<two-letter continent code(s) where the data is sourced>"], "countries": ["<ISO3 country code(s) where the data is sourced; or the string \"not applicable\"; or null — see output_instructions>"], "number_of_rows": "<number of entries/observations in the dataset, with the unit reported by the authors, summed across splits>", "demographic_info": "<which demographic attributes are available about the subjects/entities (e.g. age, gender, race/ethnicity, location, socioeconomic, language). null if none reported.>", "annotations": "<which annotations/labels are available, and their schema or label set if stated. null if none.>", "evidence": { "years_data": "<verbatim supporting quote, or null>", "license": "<verbatim supporting quote, or null>", "geographic_sourcing": "<verbatim supporting quote for continents/countries, or null>", "number_of_rows": "<verbatim supporting quote, or null>" } } ] }
